summary: Player-3 won after 6 turns by using State Swap to steal player-2's position at state A, then using Momentum to guarantee a successful transition to Victory. The game featured strategic card play with Certainty, State Swap, Catalyst, and Momentum cards all being used effectively.
balanceObservations: Game length was good at 6 turns - not too short or too long. The two-stage graph (Start -> Intermediate -> Victory) creates meaningful decisions.
State Swap proved to be a powerful card, allowing player-3 to steal player-2's hard-won position at state A. This card creates interesting counterplay opportunities.
Certainty card guarantees success but was immediately countered by State Swap, showing cards have appropriate counterplay.
Probability boosts (Catalyst +0.2, Momentum +0.3) are well-balanced. Combined with base 0.6-0.7 probabilities, they create meaningful risk management decisions without being overpowered.
All three players reached intermediate states (A, B, C) showing the initial 0.7 probability from Start is reasonable.
The 0.6 base probability for Victory transitions means players need card support to have high success rates, creating tension and strategic depth.
Random number generation worked correctly with proper success/failure outcomes based on thresholds.
